brief.concept: Cinematic music film for bZ's 'Wake Up For You (Algenib Mix)' (album Reckless Grace), a gospel-trap reveille built on Ephesians 5:14 — 'Wake up, sleeper, rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.' Algenib is the blue-white star on Pegasus's shoulder. The film follows Dai, a grief-frozen night-shift custodian who sleeps in her parked car, and the one growing star that wakes her and sends her to show mercy on a scared stranger. A recurring MOTIF — a single blue-white star that keeps GROWING (windshield to puddle to dialysis monitor to sunrise) — carries the resurrection idea. GRADE: the film opens in cold indigo/charcoal and HARD-CUTS to warm amber/gold on the first hook, then the warmth grows to a full dawn. Anamorphic, fine grain, hyperreal, dignified — hard-but-holy, never exploitative. People GROUNDED always (walk, drive, kneel, reach — never float). Hold Dai's identity across every shot via first/last-frame conditioning from one hero reference; one model for the whole film. NO superimposed HUD / floating type in-scene.
brief.mood: haunting, tender, redemptive; grief-frozen to fully-awake; cold indigo yielding to warm resurrection gold

logline: A grief-frozen night-shift custodian asleep in her car is woken by one growing blue-white star, rises from the dead of her own numbness, and carries that light to a frightened stranger — until the star becomes the dawn and she is fully awake.
synopsis: Dai sleeps against the window of her parked Civic in a sodium-lit lot, breath fogging the glass, a lone blue-white star burning in the top corner. Her phone wakes dark, then flares with four missed calls from Ate Joy, the star's reflection sliding across the glass. Her eyes snap open catching that star in the windshield — the 'rise from the dead' beat — and she steps out, a boot hitting wet asphalt where a puddle holds the star beside chalk of Pegasus on the underpass. She zips her work fleece tight over her scrubs, and on the first hook the cold breaks to warm gold: she walks an empty 5am overpass toward the skyline while the star, now hand-sized, throws amber god-rays down the road. Inside the dialysis ward she mops, then stops at an old man, Mr. Okafor, sitting awake and alone and afraid beside the humming machine; their eyes meet. She sits, takes his hand, the monitor's blue readout echoing the star, and his shoulders drop. In a stairwell she answers the phone — 'Ate?' — and laughs through tears as dawn floods the window behind her. Wide: the star has become the sun cresting between the towers, Pegasus dissolving into cloud, the city lights flicking off. On the clinic roof at true sunrise she stands fully awake, fleece off, scrubs glowing, arms loose — a resurrection without cheese. The film closes on the empty Civic, its windshield now holding the whole gold sky where one star used to be.

characters.name: Dai (Dahlia)
characters.description: Afro-Filipina woman, 34, a night-shift dialysis-clinic custodian — dignified and exhausted, grief-frozen, carrying a weight she doesn't name. Cornrows, small gold hoop earrings, a faded hospital wristband on one wrist, a navy work fleece zipped over teal scrubs. She sleeps in her parked Civic between shifts. Human eyes, real worn skin; hard-but-holy, never exploitative. Grounded always — she drives, walks, kneels, reaches; never floats. She is the emotional through-line of the film and must stay recognizably the same person in every shot.
characters.externalGoal: Get up, get through the night shift, and answer the calls she has been avoiding
characters.internalNeed: To wake from her own grief-numbness — to rise from the dead of not-feeling and let light in again
characters.contradiction: The grief makes sleep and avoidance feel safer than waking, so she stays frozen even as the star keeps calling her up
characters.voice: Nearly silent; speaks only in behavior — a held breath, a snapped-awake inhale, a hand taken, one word on a phone
vulnerabilities: the exhaustion that keeps her asleep in the car
the grief she won't pick up the phone to face
blindSpots: that someone (Ate Joy) is still reaching for her
that her own small mercy is the thing that wakes her

relationships.mr-okafor: the frightened stranger she chooses to sit with and comfort
relationships.ate-joy: the sister whose missed calls she keeps avoiding until the stairwell

characters.name: Mr. Okafor
characters.description: An elderly Black man, late 70s, alone in the dialysis ward in the small hours — awake, scared, dignified, a blanket over his knees beside the humming machine, its blue readout glowing on his face. Shown with warmth and respect, never as a prop. By the film's tender center he is the one Dai's small mercy reaches.
characters.externalGoal: Get through the long machine hours of the night without being alone
characters.internalNeed: To be seen and sat with — company instead of fear
characters.contradiction: He is too proud and too tired to ask for company, so he sits awake and alone until someone chooses to stay
characters.voice: Wordless — a frightened stillness that softens when his hand is taken
vulnerabilities: the fear of the long machine night
blindSpots: that the exhausted custodian would stop and stay for him

relationships.dai: the custodian who stops, sits, and takes his hand

locations.name: The Parking Lot
locations.description: A cold sodium-lit clinic parking lot before dawn — Dai's parked Civic, orange-grey light, breath fogging the glass, a lone blue-white star burning high in the top corner. Cold indigo/charcoal grade.

locations.name: The Underpass
locations.description: A wet 5am underpass near the lot — rain-slick asphalt holding a puddle, a chalk drawing of Pegasus on the concrete wall behind. Cold grade, the star reflected in the water.

locations.name: The Overpass
locations.description: An empty pedestrian overpass at 5am facing the city skyline — the place the cold breaks to warm gold on the first hook, the star now hand-sized throwing amber god-rays down the road. Steam-breath, hair lifting.

locations.name: The Dialysis Ward
locations.description: A quiet night dialysis ward — rows of chairs, one humming machine with a blue monitor readout, polished floor Dai mops. Where her small mercy reaches Mr. Okafor. Cool clinical light warming with the growing dawn.

locations.name: The Stairwell
locations.description: A concrete clinic stairwell with a tall window — where Dai answers the phone and laughs through tears as dawn floods in behind her.

locations.name: The Clinic Roof
locations.description: The flat clinic roof at true sunrise — where Dai stands fully awake, fleece off, scrubs glowing, the star now the sun cresting between the towers. Full warm dawn, Pegasus dissolving into cloud.

props.name: The Growing Star
props.description: A single blue-white star — the Algenib motif. It keeps GROWING across the film: a pinpoint in the windshield, a reflection in a puddle, an echo in the dialysis monitor's blue readout, then the sun itself at dawn. The visual engine of the resurrection idea.

props.name: Dai's Phone
props.description: Dai's phone on the dark dashboard — wakes with a banner 'Ate Joy (4 missed)', the star's reflection sliding across its glass; the call she finally answers in the stairwell.

props.name: The Work Fleece
props.description: Dai's navy work fleece, worn over teal scrubs — zipped tight at the pre-hook as she steadies herself, then taken OFF on the roof at sunrise when she is fully awake.

wardrobe.name: Scrubs and Work Fleece
wardrobe.description: Dai's teal clinic scrubs under a navy work fleece, cornrows, small gold hoop earrings, a faded hospital wristband — grief-worn but dignified. The fleece zips tight pre-hook and comes off at the sunrise roof, the scrubs catching the gold dawn.

scenes.title: Asleep in the Lot
scenes.narrativePurpose: Establish Dai grief-frozen and asleep in her car under one cold star, with the missed calls she is avoiding — the numbness the film will wake her from.
scenes.objective: Dai sleeps through the cold pre-dawn, avoiding the calls and the grief waiting on her phone.
scenes.opposition: Her own exhaustion and grief, which make sleep and avoidance feel safer than waking.

visibleActions.subject: dai
visibleActions.action: sleeps against the car window, breath fogging the glass, a lone blue star burning in the top corner
visibleActions.objectInteraction: rests her head against the cold window of the parked Civic
visibleActions.subtext: even asleep she is bracing; something far off is already calling her up

visibleActions.subject: dai
visibleActions.action: does not stir as her dark phone flares with a banner of four missed calls, the star's reflection sliding across the glass
visibleActions.objectInteraction: the phone lights beside her, unanswered
visibleActions.subtext: the grief she won't pick up is right there, waiting

scenes.decision: She stays asleep and unreaching rather than wake to the calls she is avoiding.
scenes.change: Dai, the cold lot, the growing star, and the unanswered calls are established; her numbness is shown as grief, not laziness.
scenes.consequence: The star brightens and the call keeps coming — the only thing left is for her to wake.
scenes.audienceLearns: A grief-frozen woman sleeps in her car under one cold star while the calls she needs to answer go unanswered.

scenes.title: Rise from the Dead
scenes.narrativePurpose: The waking — Dai's eyes snap open on the star, she steps out onto the wet underpass past Pegasus chalk, and braces herself to move.
scenes.objective: Dai must wake, get out of the car, and steady herself to begin moving toward the shift.
scenes.opposition: The pull of sleep and the weight she's carrying, and the cold wet dark she must step into.

visibleActions.objectInteraction: stares up through the windshield at the star
visibleActions.subtext: the rise-from-the-dead beat — something in her comes back to life

visibleActions.subtext: she crosses from asleep to awake, onto solid cold ground

scenes.consequence: Awake and braced, she sets out toward the clinic as the first warmth is about to break.
scenes.audienceLearns: The star wakes her; she rises from the car and braces herself to move.

scenes.title: The First Hook
scenes.narrativePurpose: The cold-to-warm breakthrough — on the first hook the grade snaps to gold and Dai walks the empty overpass toward the skyline, the star now hand-sized.
scenes.objective: Dai must cross the empty overpass toward the clinic as the light finally turns warm.
scenes.opposition: The lingering cold and weight she's walking out of, and the long empty road ahead.

visibleActions.subject: dai
visibleActions.action: walks an empty 5am overpass toward the skyline as the grade breaks from cold to warm gold, the star now hand-sized throwing amber god-rays down the road
visibleActions.objectInteraction: walks the center line of the overpass into the widening amber light
visibleActions.subtext: the breakthrough — warmth and life finally reach her

scenes.decision: She keeps walking into the warm light rather than turning back to the cold.
scenes.change: The world turns from cold indigo to warm gold around Dai as she walks toward the city.
scenes.consequence: Carried by the warmth, she arrives at the clinic ward where her mercy will be asked for.
scenes.audienceLearns: On the hook the cold breaks to gold — the light has reached her and she walks into it.

scenes.title: The Mercy
scenes.narrativePurpose: The tender center — Dai stops mopping at a frightened old man alone with the machine, sits, and takes his hand; the small mercy that is what truly wakes her.
scenes.objective: Dai must choose whether to pass by or stop for the frightened stranger alone in the ward.
scenes.opposition: Her own exhaustion and the easy option of mopping past and finishing the shift alone.

visibleActions.subject: dai

visibleActions.objectInteraction: sets the mop aside as she turns toward the old man
visibleActions.subtext: she sees him — she won't pass by

visibleActions.objectInteraction: folds her hand around his beside the glowing blue monitor
visibleActions.subtext: the small mercy that finally wakes her all the way

scenes.decision: She stops and sits with him rather than mopping past and finishing the night alone.

scenes.consequence: Having chosen mercy, she is ready to answer the calls she was avoiding.
scenes.audienceLearns: Her small mercy to a frightened stranger is the thing that truly wakes her.

scenes.title: Answer the Call
scenes.narrativePurpose: She picks up the grief at last — Dai answers Ate Joy in the stairwell and laughs through tears as dawn floods in.
scenes.objective: Dai must finally answer the sister's call she has been avoiding all night.
scenes.opposition: The grief and avoidance that kept the phone unanswered since the lot.

visibleActions.subject: dai

visibleActions.objectInteraction: lifts the phone to her ear against the bright stairwell window
visibleActions.subtext: the call she avoided all night, finally picked up — the grief met with light

scenes.decision: She answers and lets the feeling come instead of avoiding it any longer.
scenes.change: Dai answers the sister and breaks into a tearful laugh as the dawn fills the stairwell.
scenes.consequence: Unfrozen and connected again, she steps up to the roof to meet the full sunrise.
scenes.audienceLearns: She finally answers the call she was avoiding — the grief met with a tearful laugh in the light.

scenes.title: Fully Awake
scenes.narrativePurpose: The resurrection payoff — the star becomes the sun, Dai stands fully awake on the roof with the fleece off, and the film closes on her empty car holding the whole gold sky.
scenes.objective: Dai must step into the full sunrise, fully awake, and let the light hold her.
scenes.opposition: The last weight of who she was in the cold — the frozen version she is leaving behind.

visibleActions.objectInteraction: lets the taken-off fleece hang from one hand as she lifts her face to the sun
visibleActions.subtext: fully awake — risen from the dead of her own numbness, no armor left

visibleActions.objectInteraction: the empty car holds the full dawn in its glass
visibleActions.subtext: the one star has become the whole sky; she is up and gone into the day

scenes.decision: She takes off the armor and lets the full light hold her instead of bracing against it.
scenes.change: The star completes its growth into the sun and Dai stands fully awake and unarmored in the dawn.
scenes.consequence: A new, hard-won wakefulness — grief met, mercy given, the whole sky alight.
scenes.audienceLearns: The star she woke to has become the dawn, and she stands fully awake, unarmored, in the light.
